gloss: The Pillow Book (c. 1000), by Sei Shōnagon

definitions.explanation: A collection of essays, lists, and anecdotes written around the year 1000 by {清少納言|せいしょうなごん}, a lady-in-waiting at the Heian court. With its sharp observations of court life and nature, it is regarded as the first great work of the Japanese essay form, {随筆|ずいひつ}.

examples.japanese: {枕草子|まくらのそうし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{随筆|ずいひつ}→随筆：04314_zuihitsu⟧だ。
examples.english: The Pillow Book is a collection of essays.

examples.japanese: {枕草子|まくらのそうし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧はあけぼの」⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{始|はじ}まる→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
examples.english: The Pillow Book begins with "In spring, the dawn."

examples.japanese: ⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{枕草子|まくらのそうし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{冒頭|ぼうとう}→冒頭：11725_boutou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{暗記|あんき}→暗記：01701_anki⟧させられたのを⟦{覚|おぼ}えている→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧。
examples.english: I remember being made to memorize the opening of The Pillow Book in classical Japanese class.

notes:
Note the reading: ⟦{枕|まくら}→枕：03898_makura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{草子|そうし}, with an unwritten ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧はあけぼの: "In spring, the dawn" — the famous opening line, which names the best time of each season
- {清少納言|せいしょうなごん}: the author
- {三大随筆|さんだいずいひつ}: the three great classical essay collections, with {方丈記|ほうじょうき} and {徒然草|つれづれぐさ}

CULTURAL NOTE:
It is often paired with ⟦{源氏物語|げんじものがたり}→源氏物語：31025_genjimonogatari⟧, and its author with that tale's author, ⟦{紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}→紫式部：30771_murasakishikibu⟧, who served a rival empress. Its lists of "things that are delightful" and "things that are annoying" still inspire modern imitations.
